risks: Silent-catch doctrine makes every WS2 breakage invisible at runtime: a dispatcher bug that swallows a sub-hook exception disables that hook with zero symptoms. Per-subhook try/catch + the fault-isolation test are mandatory, not optional.

Diary/tool-count coupling: compact-suggester/main.js:216 incrementSharedToolCount() is the ONLY writer of the shared tool counter (diary-capture.js:62). Dropping it during the fold silently kills diary capture, Stop 'Session paused' messages, and reflect-ready pending actions.

PreCompact↔suggester state coupling: pre-compact resets the suggester state file via getSuggesterStatePath (diary-capture.js:77); if the folded counter changes its state path, suggestions survive compaction silently.

quality-check.test.js:204-229 is the only hooks.json registration test; the dispatcher restructure breaks it by design — replacing it with weaker assertions would leave future registration regressions untestable.

e2e-hooks.test.js spawns entry files directly, not via hooks.json — green e2e proves nothing about wiring; a typo'd dispatcher command in hooks.json would pass the whole suite while disabling all hooks in real sessions.

Async/sync semantics: async hooks cannot block. If observe-pre folds into the sync PreToolUse dispatcher, its fs append + daemon spawn/signal (observe/main.js:324-375) moves onto the blocking path of every tool call; if it stays async-separate, the '~6 entries' count is 7. Either way the deny path must stay sync.

Single-JSON-object protocol: each hook process may emit at most one stdout JSON object. A dispatcher merging arc-remind + compact-suggester + quality-check outputs must merge systemMessage/additionalContext fields into ONE object per event (compact-suggester and arc-remind can both fire on the same Bash event today only because they are separate processes).

In-process state assumptions break in a dispatcher: utils.js caches sessionId at module level; observe/main.js:59-63 parses ARCFORGE_OBSERVE_SKIP_PATHS 'once at module load (fresh process per event)'; getSuggesterStatePath memoization. All safe today via process-per-event; a long-lived or shared-module dispatcher must re-derive per event.

Cross-event state for WS3 autopilot denies: the PreToolUse deny reads counters written by the PostToolUse recorder (arcforge-arc-remind-test-seen / -skill-paths temp files, keyed by sessionId). A sessionId mismatch between events (setSessionIdFromInput ordering) yields deny-never-fires — silently, in unattended loops where nobody is watching.

PreToolUse denies are void under --dangerously-skip-permissions (documented in sdd-ratify-guard/main.js:12-17): dag-guard and autopilot denies are meaningless without their engine-side twins (loop.js / finish-epic.js / coordinator-core.js write paths).

Stop-time quality batching changes the feedback channel: PostToolUse additionalContext is unavailable at Stop; routing findings through Stop decision:block can loop the session (stop_hook_active), while systemMessage-only means the model never sees type errors. Also end.js currently owns Stop exclusively and calls process.exit(0) at :184 — a Stop dispatcher must sequence quality batch before/around it.

end.js O(1) change drops transcript enrichment (userMessageContent/toolsUsed/filesModified) from session JSON on below-threshold Stops — downstream consumers (learning-unification flows, inject-context resume summaries) must be checked for reliance on those fields.

arc-remind PR_BOUNDARY_RE covers `gh pr create` too; promoting it wholesale would deny PR creation in loops, not just merge/push — WS3 needs a narrower deny predicate than the existing nudge predicate.

Plugin cache: hook changes without a version bump don't propagate to the installed marketplace copy (project plugin rule) — WS2 'behavior-preserving' verification in a live session requires `claude --plugin-dir .`, not the installed plugin.

GIT_MERGE_RE extension for `git -C <path> merge` must resolve the -C target for the marker check; matching the regex but checking the wrong cwd would create false denies in the base checkout — the exact failure mode (false-positive block) the guard doctrine forbids.

ARCFORGE_DISABLED_HOOKS control plane: if a disabled guard id silently also disables the shared counter increments living in the same dispatcher pass, unrelated features (diary, compact suggestions) die with it — per-id granularity must map to sub-hooks, not dispatcher processes.
